annotation.summary_en: Three men at a cafe compete with increasingly exaggerated hunting stories involving rhinos, elephants, and buffaloes, until one man's lion encounter is revealed to be a zoo prank.
annotation.summary_detailed_en: In a brick-walled cafe setting, three men sit around a table with coffee and cigarettes, engaging in a competitive exchange of 'tall tales.' The first man, wearing a red-and-olive polo shirt, describes a terrifying hunt in Tanzania where a rhinoceros charged at him; he claims he waited until it was five meters away before shooting it between the eyes with his carbine. The second man, a heavyset man in a vest, counters with a story from India where he supposedly shot a charging elephant at a distance of only three meters. Not to be outdone, the first man recounts another tale of a buffalo with sinus issues that he shot from just one meter away. Finally, a thin man in black interrupts, claiming he once faced a lion from only half a meter away. When asked if he shot it, he reveals he simply spat on it. The punchline arrives when he explains the consequence: he wasn't a brave hunter in the wild, but was simply beaten up by zoo security for harassing the animals.
catchphrases: Ինչ պտի ըլնի գազանանոցի աշխատողներով բռնին տփին
